race_context: New Palestine Community Schools, formerly the Community School Corporation of Southern Hancock County, is based in New Palestine in Hancock County {npcs_history}{npcs_supt}. It runs Little Dragons Early Childhood, three elementary schools (Brandywine, New Palestine and Sugar Creek), New Palestine Junior High and New Palestine High School {npcs_supt}. Public School Review, using federal and state data, lists about 3,959 students in six schools {psr_enroll}. Superintendent: Dr. Gina Pleak {npcs_supt}.

The board has five members, each tied to a numbered district: Amanda Wooton (District 1), Laura Haeberle (District 2), Jon Hooker (District 3, vice president), Dan Walker (District 4, president) and Brian McKinney (District 5, secretary) {npcs_board}. District 3 represents all of Sugar Creek Township, which is made up of Districts 1 and 2 {npcs_board}{indystar_2022}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 3 and District 5, one seat each, matching the state list {in_list}. Hooker, appointed to District 3 in August 2020 and on the board since, is not on the 2026 ballot, so Emily Boesen (Republican) and Brian Hart (Independent) are competing for an open seat {indystar_2022}{npcs_history}{in_list}. McKinney, District 5 member since 2007, is running unopposed {npcs_history}{in_list}.

Building consolidation (announced March 2026): Hoodline, an AI-assisted news site summarizing district materials, reported that the district would close and remove the junior high building, move grades 6-8 into the intermediate school campus renamed New Palestine Junior High starting in 2026-27, use the cleared site to expand Sugar Creek Elementary, and serve kindergarten through grade 5 in the three elementary schools {hoodline_jh}. It reported that the district cited lower operating costs from running fewer buildings and named Senate Enrolled Act 1, the 2025 property-tax law, as a budget pressure {hoodline_jh}.
Upcoming board business: the Oct. 26, 2026 meeting agenda includes budget approval and ratification of the teachers' master contract {npcs_board}.
Recognition: the district reported in August 2026 that it was named a 2026 Top Workplace and in September 2026 that it received a 'Best in Education' recognition {npcs_news}.

Forums: this guide found no candidate forum or questionnaire for the District 3 race that it could read. The Daily Reporter in Greenfield published a story on the race on Sept. 22, 2026, but its site was not accessible to this guide.
